However, Min-Max scaler was found to be the most reliable scaling approach. 5.1.5 Train Model This section covers the first objective of Application 1, which entails process modelling using data-driven models, with the models including SPB and WNS flow rates and other features to accurately model ESS. This was performed in two major steps as detailed in the following sections. In brief, the project team used a minimal feature set (high-frequency features that have at least 50% of the days available) at first to compare 10 different algorithms. Following, the top performing algorithms were selected and were carried out through a rigorous feature selection and hyperparameter optimization. Finally, one model was selected and re-trained on the entire dataset to be used for deployment. In all cases, nested cross-validation (nested CV) was used. Nested CV is an incremental learning approach where learning happens at multiple levels or stages, building upon each other incrementally. Nested CV was selected due to the small sample to features ratio in this dataset. More than 120 features were candidates to be tested and only 866 instances (days) were available with a very high missingness rate (exceeded 50% in many days). Another reason for this selection was the stochastic nature of the data and inconsistent variation in ESS over the examined period. Nested CV provides a robust technique that allows the use of the entire dataset in training and testing while minimizing bias and overfitting. It employs two layers of CV: an outer loop for model evaluation and an inner loop for feature selection and hyperparameter tuning. In the outer loop, the dataset is partitioned into multiple folds (5 or 10 folds in this study), with each fold being held out in turn as a test set while the remaining folds form the training set. Within this training set, the inner loop conducts another round of CV (5 or 10 folds in this study) to optimize hyperparameters, tune model architecture, and select features. This process is repeated for each fold in the outer loop, ensuring a comprehensive and unbiased evaluation. In the first two steps, the inner loops (5-fold CV) were used for the selection of algorithms used and feature selection. Subsequently, in the last step, selected models and their selected features were used for hyperparameter optimization using the inner loops (10-fold CV) and final models with different imbalance treatment methods were compared based on the testing results from the outer loops (10-fold CV). 5.1.5.1 Preliminary Model Selection To perform preliminary algorithm selection, a certain dataset with selected features needs to be used. This was performed by selecting features with a missing ratio of more than 50% (at least 50% of the days are available). The goal here was to define a starting point to decide on the algorithms to be used. Using this dataset, ten different algorithms were compared to model the HR-CS process.
